Apple's annual September iPhone launch event is still about two months away, but this year will be different. In September, Apple will not unveil the entire iPhone lineup at once — only the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and a brand-new foldable iPhone will be released first.

The iPhone lineup keeps growing

Over the past few years, the annual iPhone lineup has gradually expanded. Not long ago, only three new models were launched each year: the iPhone 11, iPhone 11 Pro, and iPhone 11 Pro Max. By 2020, with the addition of the iPhone 12 mini, the number of models released annually rose to four; in 2022, the iPhone 12 mini was replaced by the iPhone 14 Plus, which was later succeeded by the iPhone Air.

With the arrival of the iPhone 16e, the number of models released each year has further grown to five. Once the iPhone Ultra launches, the annual iPhone lineup will expand to six models. That's quite a lot of models — if all were unveiled at once, the stage would be very crowded.

Therefore, Apple has decided to adopt a staggered release strategy instead.

Two iPhone launch events: fall and spring

The iPhone 18 lineup will include six models: iPhone 18, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2, and iPhone Ultra.

The logic behind this staggered strategy is clear: flagship models launch in the fall, while mid- and lower-tier models debut in the spring. The specific arrangement is as follows:

  • Fall 2026: iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone Ultra
  • Spring 2027: iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2

When the iPhone lineup expanded to four models, the fourth model always disappointed in terms of sales — whether it was the iPhone mini or the iPhone Plus. So Apple believes it makes sense to clearly separate the lineup and give the additional models their own moment in the spotlight.

But when it comes to the iPhone 18, the situation will change slightly. Reports suggest Apple is working to unify the production processes for the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, so the differences between the two phones may be significantly narrowed.

It remains unclear whether this will bring major upgrades to the iPhone 18e or lead to downgrades for the iPhone 18 — but the distinction between the two phones may ultimately come down to details such as the display panel and cameras.

Summary

In summary, assuming the iPhone Air isn't eventually discontinued (which I certainly hope won't happen) — this will be the new landscape for the iPhone lineup going forward. Three models in the fall, three in the spring. The ultimate goal is to allow Apple to better spread out its release schedule and get products into the hands of the right consumers.

Another possible outcome is that the average selling price of iPhones will rise, because any consumer wanting to ride the wave of new hardware will have no choice but to buy the iPhone 18 Pro, rather than a more affordable model.

Whether a staggered launch can truly drive sales across all models remains to be seen, but these are the initial thoughts.

What are your thoughts on Apple staggering its iPhone releases? Will you buy a new iPhone in the fall, or wait until spring? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
